T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) — YES (DPA-backed refinery capacity expansion, new Brownsville refinery, Venezuelan crude supply ramp-up)

**Synopsis:**
The White House is exploring use of the Defense Production Act to expand U.S. oil refining capacity in response to fuel price surges linked to an Iran conflict. Refiners, running at ~98% utilization, favor efficiency upgrades over new builds. The administration is simultaneously pursuing foreign crude access, notably via a government equity stake in a Venezuelan oil venture. A proposed new 168,000 bpd refinery in Brownsville, TX — with ties to Trump family and administration figures — has emerged as a focal test case. The push is politically motivated by midterm election pressures and longer-term energy security concerns.
